formValues.pipRepositioningDetails: Conversion and renovation projects considered; PIP scope aligned with brand standards and market. New-build and expansion also considered.

operationalSupport.keyMoneyPaymentTiming: Upon opening or at signing; may vary by deal.
operationalSupport.keyMoneyPaymentStructure: Pro rata repayment if terminated within 5–7 years; terms vary by agreement.
operationalSupport.keyMoneyClawbackTerms: Often 50% at LOI/brand approval, 50% at opening; negotiated.
operationalSupport.serviceDifferentiators: Comprehensive revenue management, sales and marketing, accounting, procurement, HR, technology, design, and development support per brand standards.
operationalSupport.decisionMaking: Owner approvals typically required for capital expenditures, major contracts, and budget variances. Brand approval for standards and PIP scope.
operationalSupport.disputeResolution: Escalation path from GM to regional to corporate. Mediation available. Typical resolution within 30–60 days for standard issues.
operationalSupport.industryRecognition: Brand standards, reporting, training, and support resources.
operationalSupport.specializations: Full-service and select-service segments; conversions and new builds; urban and suburban markets.
operationalSupport.testimonials: Multiple successful conversions and new-build openings in key markets. Owner references available upon request.
operationalSupport.ownerPortalFeatures: Monthly P&L, budget vs. actual, forecasts, operational metrics, brand standards, and support resources.
operationalSupport.ownerPortalNotes: Web-based portal with monthly financials, brand standards library, and pipeline reporting. Access to regional owner relations.
operationalSupport.ongoingSupportIncluded: Revenue management support, sales and marketing resources, accounting and financial reporting, procurement services, HR and training, technology support, design and renovation guidance, and development services per brand standards.
operationalSupport.crsParticipation: Full participation in brand CRS; central reservation system integration required for all properties.
operationalSupport.gdsParticipation: Yes; brand participates in major GDS channels (Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) for distribution.

legalTerms.aopRestrictions: No same-brand hotel within AOP during Term

legalTerms.terminationForCause: Pro rata repayment if terminated within 3 years
legalTerms.terminationWithoutCause: Pro rata repayment if terminated within 3 years
legalTerms.terminationOnSale: Pro rata repayment if terminated within 3 years
legalTerms.liquidatedDamages: 1.5x annual royalty fee or fixed amount if terminated early
legalTerms.loiNonBinding: All other terms pending execution of definitive agreements

legalTerms.conditionsPrecedent: Subject to approval by franchisor's development committee, successful site review, financials, and legal diligence.

legalTerms.assignmentRestrictions: Assignment permitted to qualified transferee with brand approval. Transferee must assume all obligations. Notice and approval process required.

blocks.title: Independent Soft-Brand Conversion
blocks.body: Curio creates owner value on distinctive independents that need Hilton Honors distribution without a hard-brand prototype—affiliation fits when local story, design character, and F&B identity are assets owners want to preserve while meeting collection standards.

blocks.title: Resort or Experiential Repositioning
blocks.body: Resort or experiential assets suit Curio when place and programming already sell, and Hilton mainly sharpens demand—owners underwrite PIP, labor, and F&B intensity carefully so soft-brand cutover is not mistaken for light capital work.

blocks.title: Heritage Adaptive Reuse
blocks.body: Historic or character buildings fit Curio when architecture is the product and Hilton commercial tools can monetize it—sponsors protect how much local identity survives brand review while rooms and public spaces meet collection thresholds.

blocks.title: Third-Party Operator-Led
blocks.body: Curio suits assets run by experienced operators who balance Hilton collection QA with local execution—sponsors need affiliation lift, financing credibility, and Honors scale while keeping the property's story intact after cutover.

blocks.title: Demand pattern
blocks.body: Curio demand follows market seasonality plus Honors campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional only.

blocks.title: Competitive pressure
blocks.body: Sister brands can both help and cannibalize. Map same-parent density before assuming exclusive Honors capture for Curio.

blocks.title: Economics overview
blocks.body: Owner economics for Curio Collection by Hilton combine parent fee schedules (Dealality educational fee framework) with Curio operating intensity. Educational fee buckets are not negotiated deal terms.

blocks.title: Pre-opening cash
blocks.body: Pre-opening cash covers PIP/conversion, FF&E, pre-opening payroll, and brand-required openings support. Size to the asset’s conversion scope.

blocks.title: Ramp
blocks.body: Ramp assumes Honors channels turn on cleanly. If systems or product delivery lag, Curio ramp elongates.

blocks.title: Steady state
blocks.body: Steady-state GOP depends on labor, F&B (if any), elite fulfillment, and market ADR — platform fees are only one line.

blocks.title: Renewal / exit
blocks.body: Renewal and exit economics depend on contract terms, PIP catch-up, and reflag options—confirm in the deal file.

blocks.title: Opening process
blocks.body: Opening is a systems + product + people cutover. Curio brand standards and Honors posting must be rehearsal-ready before opening.

blocks.title: Primary risks
blocks.body: Key risks: conversion/PIP under-scope, sister-brand density, elite fulfillment cost, and weak local demand for the Curio product story.

blocks.title: Mitigations
blocks.body: Mitigate with honest competitive-set mapping, PIP scope lock, systems cutover rehearsal, and loyalty fulfillment SOPs before opening.

blocks.title: Negotiability
blocks.body: Fees, territories, and PIP scope are deal-specific. Treat brochure ranges as educational—not as the signed economics.

blocks.title: P&L implications
blocks.body: Honors mix can stabilize direct demand for Curio but elite fulfillment is a controllable cost. Model loyalty contribution after fulfillment.

blocks.title: Operations implications
blocks.body: Front office must operationalize Honors recognition consistently. Inconsistent delivery shows up as reviews and account friction.

blocks.title: Systems implications
blocks.body: CRS/PMS loyalty posting and digital arrival tools must work on day one for Curio—systems lag erases Honors value.

blocks.title: Growth style
blocks.body: Curio growth is typically conversion- and pipeline-led within the parent system. Confirm live footprint before citing expansion narratives.

blocks.title: Footprint note
blocks.body: Treat open/pipeline figures as Brand Footprint-scoped. Absence in one region is not a global zero for Curio.
None attached

blocks.title: Owner experience
blocks.body: Expect brand standards, quality audits, and commercial onboarding for Curio. Owner experience is partnership intensity—not a hands-off affiliation.

brandPositioning: Curated collection of independent upper-upscale hotels, each with distinct character and story.
brandCustomerPromise: Independent hotels with distinct character and story under Hilton.
brandValueProposition: Retain independent hotel character while participating in Hilton distribution and Hilton Honors. Owners should confirm conversion scope, operating obligations, and participation costs directly for the asset.
companyHistory: Launched 2014; Hilton's upper-upscale collection; independent hotels.
guestPsychographics: Travelers seeking independent hotels with distinct character, local story, and reliable upper-upscale service—willing to choose a soft collection when individuality and Hilton distribution both matter.
keyBrandDifferentiators: Each property retains unique identity; Hilton loyalty reach; soft-collection flexibility for distinctive upper-upscale hotels. Confirm design and service expectations in brand engagement.
brandProfileAnalysis: Historic urban conversions, destination resorts, nature lodges, golf and beach properties, and selective new-build in sought-after markets where guests pay for one-of-a-kind character, culinary moments, and local authenticity—not commodity limited-service or economy extended-stay.
brandStandardsIntro: Curio Collection by Hilton standards vary by conversion path, F&B program, and agreement vintage. Use the table as a planning checklist—confirm every row in the commercial agreement materials, design manual, and commercial proposal before capital commitments.
questionsOwnersShouldAsk:
Which design standards apply to this address?
What is mandatory at opening vs. phased 12–24 months?
How do restaurant, bar, and kitchen requirements change PIP?
What Hilton Honors and technology cutover dates are contractual?
What QA fees apply at opening and annually?
